svg.aria-label: Storing medicinal herbs: four kinds of spoilage. Mould shows as white, green or black fuzz or spots on the surface and a musty smell; it mostly affects herbs rich in sugar, starch or mucilage; causes are about 20-35°C, damp air and herbs not fully dried; prevent it by drying thoroughly, sealing against damp, storing somewhere cool and re-drying in the sun regularly. Insect damage shows as bore holes, insect dust and webbing; it mostly affects herbs rich in starch, sugar or protein, and animal medicines; prevent it by keeping herbs dry and sealed, and by re-drying in the sun or baking at low heat. Oiling (fanyou) shows as a sticky, darkened, oily surface with a rancid smell; it mostly affects oily and sugary herbs; prevent it with cool, dark, sealed storage, without crushing, and do not store too long. Fading and loss of aroma show as colour turning dull and brown and scent growing faint; it mostly affects flowers, leaves and aromatic herbs; prevent it with dark, sealed, cool storage, and replace flowers and leaves after about 1 year. Storage conditions: cool, ideally not above about 20-25°C; relative humidity below about 75%; dark; storeroom ventilated but containers sealed; off the floor and away from walls. Lime jar: quicklime wrapped in cloth at the bottom, a wooden board or bamboo mat in between, herbs on top, lid on tight; quicklime gets very hot when it meets water, so wrap it well, set it firmly and keep children away. Containers: clay or china jars are the traditional first choice; glass lets light in, so keep it in the dark; tin keeps out damp and rodents but is not for strongly acidic herbs; cloth and paper bags are for short-term use only; thick plastic bags only for fully dried herbs, tied tight inside a second bag. Check every 1-2 months, and throw away the whole bag if it is mouldy
svg.title: Storing medicinal herbs

g.text: Storing herbs: preventing mould, insects, oiling and fading
Badly stored herbs lose their effect at best; at worst they go mouldy and form toxins
(such as aflatoxins, which boiling does not destroy)
Dark: in the dark or in opaque containers
Airy: ventilate the storeroom, but keep
Off floor and walls: on shelves or pallets,

text.tspan: ⚠️ Quicklime gets very hot with water:

g.text: wrap it well, set it firmly, keep children away;
if it gets in the eyes, brush off the solid first,
then rinse with plenty of clean water
Charcoal or dry rice husks also absorb damp,
❌ If it is mouldy, throw away the whole bag:
do not wash it, sun it or stir-fry it and then use it
Check every 1-2 months as a rule; check monthly in the plum-rain season, in humid
huinantian spells (warm damp air from the south) and before and after the rainy season;
take out anything gone damp and re-dry it in the sun or at low heat; first in, first out
Store toxic herbs separately, labelled "Toxic", locked away or up high,
never together with ordinary herbs or food
